opportunities.title: Joint Center of Excellence for Advanced Materials Research
opportunities.summary: This is technically relevant to METSS advanced materials and testing capabilities, especially composite/adhesive durability and environmental-performance research. It is not a direct METSS prime opportunity based on the stated eligibility restriction to COE member universities. Recommend partner-oriented investigation only after confirming that an active, open project call exists and that an eligible university can include METSS under acceptable cost-share and teaming terms.
opportunities.why: The opportunity addresses research and engineering related to composites and advanced materials in commercial aircraft, including bonded-joint durability, environmental aging, additive manufacturing, crashworthiness, lightning effects, new material systems, and maintenance/inspection.: These areas align with METSS public capabilities in polymers, composite resins, coatings, adhesives, harsh-environment materials, and materials-performance testing. (Official Grants.gov record — synopsis) METSS has public advanced-materials capability relevant to composite and adhesive-material research.: The profile lists polymers, rubbers, composite resins, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, and materials for harsh environments. (Approved METSS public profile — Advanced materials) METSS has public testing and validation capabilities relevant to durability, environmental exposure, performance, and materials compatibility work.: The profile lists chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing, plus analytical and environmental testing capabilities. (Approved METSS public profile — Testing and validation; facilities)
opportunities.action: Contact the FAA COE/JAMS point of contact or the COE university leads to confirm whether an active project-specific call is open, identify the applicable topic deadline, and verify whether a non-member company may participate as a subcontractor or research partner. Do not allocate proposal resources until those points and cost-share terms are confirmed.
opportunities.eligibility: CONDITIONAL: The official record limits applicants to member universities of the Joint Center of Excellence. METSS Corporation is described in the approved profile as an applied R&D company, not a member university. METSS therefore is not shown eligible to apply directly. A role supporting an eligible COE university may be possible, but the record does not establish subcontractor, research-partner, or cost-share rules for METSS. Blocking or unverified requirements: Direct applicant must be a member university of the COE.; Active project-specific submission timing and requirements are not provided in the supplied Grants.gov record.; Any required cost share and METSS's ability or willingness to provide it are unknown.; An eligible COE university partner and its ability to include METSS are not established.

opportunities.title: Process Systems, Reaction Engineering, and Molecular Thermodynamics
opportunities.summary: This is a technically adjacent NSF fundamental-research opportunity, particularly for reactive polymer processing, specialized chemical materials, and experimental validation tied to a genuinely new engineering-science question. METSS's public profile supports chemistry, polymers, process scale-up, and testing, but does not establish the core theory, modeling, or academic research infrastructure emphasized by the program. The unrestricted applicant-type field supports entity-type eligibility, but PAPPG compliance, staffing, and proposal readiness remain unknown. Investigate only if METSS can identify a fundamental research concept and an academically strong research partner; do not position a routine process-development or scale-up project as responsive.
opportunities.why: The program supports fundamental research in chemical reaction engineering, process systems, reactive polymer processing, and molecular thermodynamics, including chemical reactors, sustainable manufacturing, modular systems, and functional polymer materials.: The synopsis identifies reactor design, reactive polymer processing, molecular thermodynamics, process modeling/control, sustainable manufacturing, and tailored functional materials as program areas. (Official Grants.gov record — Synopsis) METSS has public capabilities relevant to polymer materials, chemistry, formulation, reaction characterization, process design, pilot-scale work, and materials testing.: The profile documents polymers, resins, coatings, specialty chemistry, sample analysis, reaction characterization, product/process design, pilot-scale operations, and chemical/materials testing. (Approved METSS public profile — capabilities) METSS has some adjacent public past performance in advanced polymer materials and chemical production.: Examples include Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials (W911QY-23-P-0038), DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production (FA8650-24-2-5555), and Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors (SP4701-22-P-0054). (Approved METSS public profile — public past performance examples)
opportunities.action: Before investing in a proposal, identify a university research partner and prepare a one-page fundamental research concept that clearly separates the work from process development. Contact the NSF Program Director to validate topical fit and request the current applicable submission/target-date guidance. Internally verify NSF/PAPPG submission readiness, PI/team availability, budget capacity, and METSS's desired role.
opportunities.eligibility: CONDITIONAL: The Grants.gov record lists applicant type as unrestricted, with no additional eligibility text, so METSS Corporation is not excluded by the published entity-type field. However, eligibility for submission and award remains conditional on compliance with the NSF PAPPG and any program-specific proposal requirements, which the approved METSS profile does not establish. Blocking or unverified requirements: NSF PAPPG-compliant proposal preparation and submission requirements are not evidenced in the METSS public profile.; The proposed work must fit the program's fundamental, hypothesis-driven engineering-research scope; the record expressly states that process-development proposals are not appropriate.; A qualified PI, research team, budget, and available proposal resources are unknown.

opportunities.title: State Veterans Home Construction Grant Program
opportunities.summary: This is a large VA infrastructure grant program for eligible State and Tribal governments to construct or renovate veterans nursing, domiciliary, and adult day health-care facilities. METSS has only peripheral technical relevance through advanced materials and domestic manufacturing. The explicit applicant restriction is dispositive: METSS cannot prime or apply directly. No defined work package supports a meaningful subcontractor recommendation from the supplied record.
opportunities.why: Only State and Tribal Governments may apply; private organizations are expressly excluded.: States: "ONLY STATE AND TRIBAL GOVERNMENTS MAY APPLY" and "NO PRIVATE ORGANIZATION... IS QUALIFIED TO APPLY." (Official Grants.gov record — additionalEligibility) The grant supports construction or renovation of State/Tribal-owned and operated skilled nursing, domiciliary, and adult day health care facilities.: The program funds construction/renovation of veterans extended-care facilities, rather than R&D or procurement of METSS-developed products. (Official Grants.gov record — fundingActivityDescription and synopsis) Adult Day Health Care, bed replacement, and new-construction applications require a space-program analysis; supplied forms identify facility-room square-footage categories.: The included forms require proposed square footage for administrative, clinical, therapy, storage, utility, and related facility spaces. The nursing/domiciliary form also includes bed units and bathing/toilet facilities. (Included attachment: Form 10-0388-3 Space Program Analysis-Nursing Home and Domiciliary.pdf; Form 10-0388-4 Space Program Analysis-Adult Day Health Care.pdf)
opportunities.action: Do not allocate capture or proposal resources. Log as ineligible for METSS direct pursuit. Monitor only if a known eligible State/Tribal facility project separately releases a defined subcontract or supplier need that matches METSS capabilities; verify the current VA application cycle and project-specific requirements at that time.
opportunities.eligibility: NO: METSS Corporation is not an eligible direct applicant. METSS is identified in the approved profile as an applied R&D company. opportunities.title: The Genesis Mission:  Transforming Science and Energy with AI
opportunities.summary: This is a strong strategic and moderate technical-adjacency opportunity for METSS, particularly around AI-enabled chemical manufacturing, materials processing, critical-minerals processing, and materials qualification. METSS's public profile supports a substantive materials/chemistry, experimental-validation, and pilot-scale/manufacturing role—not the AI-model lead role. However, current pursuit strength is low because the ordinary FY26 submission deadlines have passed, the December 17 route is limited to FY26 Phase I awardees, and METSS's AI, data, team, cost-share, and compliance readiness are unproven. Monitor for the stated FY27 amendment or replacement opportunity while developing a compliant lab-plus-industry team.
opportunities.why: The opportunity seeks AI-enabled scientific-discovery and R&D workflows across advanced manufacturing, critical materials, energy, and other science domains.: The synopsis identifies advanced manufacturing, critical materials, and energy among the topic areas and states that teams will use novel AI models and frameworks to accelerate R&D workflows. (Official Grants.gov record, synopsis for DE-FOA-0003612) Relevant technical lanes include agentic AI-driven chemical manufacturing, AI-driven materials processing, critical-minerals extraction and processing, and AI-enabled materials discovery/development/qualification.: These focus areas align with METSS public capabilities in specialty chemistry, polymers/composites/coatings, process design, pilot-scale operations, light manufacturing, and testing. (Attachment: DE-FOA-0003612.000003.pdf, Section III, Topics 1, 3, and 12) METSS has publicly documented chemistry, functional-fluid, advanced-materials, engineering, scale-up, testing, and domestic critical-chemical capabilities.: The profile lists formulation/product development, polymers and coatings, mechanical and chemical engineering, pilot-scale/light manufacturing, advanced analytical and environmental testing, and public DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production contract FA8650-24-2-5555. (Approved METSS Public Profile v2026-07-21-public-v1)
opportunities.action: Within one business week, verify internally whether METSS received a FY26 Phase I Genesis Mission award and whether it has an approved AI/data/laboratory partner. If not, do not invest in a December 17 Phase II application; instead, contact GenesisMissionNOFO@science.doe.gov only to clarify whether any late or FY27 pathway is available, and begin FY27 teaming around one narrowly defined METSS-led experimental/materials work package with quantitative AI-advantage metrics.
opportunities.eligibility: CONDITIONAL: METSS is technically relevant as a U.S.-based applied R&D company with materials, chemistry, testing, and scale-up capabilities, but the only stated remaining FY26 deadline—December 17, 2026—is specifically for Phase II applications resulting from FY26 Phase I awards. The approved METSS profile does not establish that METSS holds a FY26 Phase I Genesis Mission award. The RFA also says DOE may decline post-deadline applications without review. evidence.support: The record lists December 17, 2026, but the RFA specifies that date for Phase II applications resulting from FY26 Phase I awards. Original FY26 Phase I and direct FY26 Phase II deadlines were May 1 and May 19, 2026, respectively.

evidence.claim: The supplied sample OT and project-agreement document establishes substantial data-rights, IP, domestic-performance, and security obligations if an award is negotiated.
evidence.source: Attachment: Sample OT and Project Agreements for DE-FOA-0003612 REV2.pdf
evidence.support: Sample terms require a project agreement, data/IP-rights certifications for delivered models and data, U.S. performance absent waiver, RTES controls, invention reporting, and flowdown obligations. The samples also show that terms remain subject to award negotiation.

gaps: No public evidence that METSS currently develops, trains, validates, or deploys AI/ML models, agentic workflows, digital twins, foundation models, or HPC-enabled scientific software.
No identified DOE/NNSA National Laboratory, Scientific User Facility, university, AI developer, data owner, or other committed partner.
No evidence that METSS is eligible for the remaining December 17 Phase II route through an FY26 Phase I Genesis Mission award.

No public evidence of available proprietary or non-proprietary datasets suitable for AI curation, associated data rights, model-component licensing rights, or American Science Cloud deployment rights.
No evidence of a data-management/sharing plan, AI safety plan, model/data cards, provenance records, red-team approach, or secure approved cloud/HPC environment.
No verified capacity for required for-profit cost share, proposal budget, indirect-rate basis, personnel availability, or computing allocation.
No verified SAM/UEI status, ownership/RTES posture, export-control constraints, or current compliance representations.
partner_needs: DOE/NNSA National Laboratory or Scientific User Facility partner for required team composition, access to DOE datasets/facilities, and potential American Science Cloud integration.
AI/HPC partner with demonstrated scientific ML, digital-twin, agentic-workflow, model-evaluation, data-engineering, and cybersecurity capabilities.
University or nonprofit research partner for domain-science modeling, scientific validation, and workforce/research depth, especially if pursuing a future Phase I team.

Industrial end user or manufacturer able to supply operational process data, define measurable deployment metrics, and support validation/transition; this is especially important for applied manufacturing or chemical-process proposals.
Data-rights and IP counsel/lead to establish a compliant project agreement, artifact register, data provenance, data-use terms, and protected-data/open-data strategy.
analysis.summary: This is a strong strategic and moderate technical-adjacency opportunity for METSS, particularly around AI-enabled chemical manufacturing, materials processing, critical-minerals processing, and materials qualification. METSS's public profile supports a substantive materials/chemistry, experimental-validation, and pilot-scale/manufacturing role—not the AI-model lead role. However, current pursuit strength is low because the ordinary FY26 submission deadlines have passed, the December 17 route is limited to FY26 Phase I awardees, and METSS's AI, data, team, cost-share, and compliance readiness are unproven. Monitor for the stated FY27 amendment or replacement opportunity while developing a compliant lab-plus-industry team.
analysis.immediate_action: Within one business week, verify internally whether METSS received a FY26 Phase I Genesis Mission award and whether it has an approved AI/data/laboratory partner. If not, do not invest in a December 17 Phase II application; instead, contact GenesisMissionNOFO@science.doe.gov only to clarify whether any late or FY27 pathway is available, and begin FY27 teaming around one narrowly defined METSS-led experimental/materials work package with quantitative AI-advantage metrics.
caveats: Assessment is based only on the supplied official Grants.gov record, the supplied RFA PDF, the supplied Sample OT and Project Agreements PDF, and the approved METSS public profile.
The attached Excel templates are listed in the Grants.gov record but their contents were not supplied as parsed text and are not relied upon here.
The Sample OT and Project Agreements document is a sample, not a final award; actual milestones, data rights, patent terms, protection periods, payment method, and negotiated scope may differ.
Several listed focus areas explicitly did not accept Phase II applications in FY26; relevance to a topic does not establish that the topic remains open or that METSS is eligible.
DOE stated that it may amend the RFA or issue an alternative funding opportunity for FY27; that future competition, timing, topics, and terms are not yet established.

opportunities.title: Critical Minerals and Materials Accelerator Notice of Funding Opportunity
opportunities.summary: DE-FOA-0003589 is strategically adjacent to METSS's domestic critical-chemicals, applied chemistry, pilot-scale, and testing capabilities, but the published topic scopes are specialized critical-minerals processing areas not evidenced in the approved METSS profile. METSS is not currently supported as a credible prime for a standalone submission. A limited testing, validation, process-development, or scale-up support role may be worth investigating only if a qualified CMM technology lead needs those capabilities and the unreveiwed NOFO requirements permit the proposed team structure. Timing in the official record: LOI deadline is April 24, 2026; Topic Area 1 full application deadline is May 29, 2026; Topic Area 2 is June 25, 2026; and Topic Area 3 is July 23, 2026. Submissions are through DOE eXCHANGE under separate Topic Area opportunity numbers, not through Grants.gov.
opportunities.why: The NOFO seeks collaborative industry partnerships to prototype and pilot bench-scale critical-minerals-and-materials processing technologies, with validation, benchmarking, industry-relevant testing, technoeconomic analysis, life-cycle assessment, and a domestic-commercialization path.: This creates a possible supporting role for METSS in testing, validation, formulation/process development, pilot-scale work, or scale-up, contingent on fit to a qualified minerals-processing technology. (Official Grants.gov synopsis, DE-FOA-0003589) The active technical scopes are materials recovery from manufacturing/postconsumer/mixed scrap; semiconductor-grade gallium, gallium nitride, germanium, and silicon-carbide refining/alloying; and direct lithium extraction, separation, processing, and associated pretreatment/disposal technologies.: METSS's approved profile does not identify direct experience in critical-mineral recovery, rare-earth processing, semiconductor-material refining, gallium/germanium/silicon-carbide processing, or direct lithium extraction. (Official Grants.gov synopsis, DE-FOA-0003589) METSS publicly describes chemical engineering, laboratory-to-commercial product/process design, pilot-scale operations, light manufacturing, and analytical, environmental, physical, and materials-compatibility testing.: These capabilities could support process validation or pilot activities, but do not by themselves prove suitability for the specified CMM processing technologies. (Approved METSS public profile, Engineering and manufacturing scale-up; Testing and validation capabilities)
opportunities.action: Obtain and review the current MOD0002 NOFO attachment—especially Section II.A, Topic-specific performance metrics, cost-share rules, LOI requirements, and team/lead-applicant rules—before any outreach. In parallel, use the listed eXCHANGE Teaming Partner List (TPL-0000069) to identify a technology lead whose defined scope needs METSS testing, validation, pilot/process-development, or scale-up support; do not commit METSS as prime or represent eligibility until internal verification is complete.
